summary: The portfolio-page timeouts (INC-002, SEV-2) were caused by config change cfg-2207, which reduced portfolio-service's DB connection-pool max_size from 50 to 5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z; pre-change concurrency (~11.4-12.4 avg, max 13.3 connections in use) already exceeded the new ceiling by ~2.3x, so the pool saturated at exactly 5 (active=5, idle=0, waiters 22-57), requests queued and hit Hikari's hard 3000ms acquire timeout, portfolio-service p99 stepped to ~4.1-4.3s, and api-gateway faithfully reported 504 upstream timeouts on /v1/portfolio/*. Confidence in this root cause is high (0.86, critic-accepted). The reporter's suspicion - the 08:00Z gateway HTTP/2 envoy upgrade dep-5220 - is rejected: it precedes the true onset by ~1h52m with no rollback, gateway CPU and p99 were flat until 09:53/09:54Z, the 504s are attributed downstream to portfolio-service, and a transport change cannot produce JDBC pool exhaustion pinned at the new ceiling. Shared ledger-db/redis-cache degradation is contradicted: slow_queries, CPU and replication lag are flat, redis connected_clients is flat, and ledger-db connections_active decreased (61.8 -> 54.5, the wrong direction). The immediate mitigation is to revert cfg-2207.

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service DB connection-pool shrink (cfg-2207) exhausted the pool
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-2207 set portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 09:52:00Z ('cost-optimisation profile small', author infra-automation). Pre-change baseline concurrency (~11.4-12.4 avg, max 13.3 connections in use) already EXCEEDED 5 by ~2.3x, so the reduced ceiling caps the pool below unchanged demand. The Hikari pool saturates (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting 22-57), acquire attempts queue and hit the hard 3000ms timeout; portfolio-service latency steps to ~4.1-4.3s and api-gateway faithfully reports 504 upstream timeouts on /v1/portfolio/*. The recorded 09:48 onset of F8 is a coarser-bucket edge artifact: at 1-minute resolution the gateway is flat through 09:53:00Z and steps at 09:54:00Z (F32), portfolio-service p99 steps at 09:53:00Z (F34), both AFTER cfg-2207's 09:52:00Z stamp. The pool shrink is the last and only change on the portfolio path immediately at onset; it is not amplification of an upstream slowdown (request_rate flat, waiting bounded, in_use pinned exactly at the new ceiling, ledger-db/redis-cache flat).

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2207 applied to portfolio-service: db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5 at 09:52:00Z; it is the last and only change to a portfolio-path service at onset, and the only portfolio-service config change in the entire 06:00-11:59Z window
Baseline DB concurrency was ~11.4-12.4 (max 13.3) before the change, i.e. ~2.3x the new ceiling of 5, so the cap alone pulls provisioned capacity below unchanged demand

Pool ceiling collapses to 5; db_pool_in_use pins at exactly 5.0 (max 5) from 09:55Z onward with zero idle and a bounded waiter queue of 22-57 (09:50Z partial bucket avg 9.17/max 12.22 brackets the rebuild to within minutes of the stamp)

Queued acquire attempts hit Hikari's hard 3000ms per-acquire timeout; zero ERROR-level pool logs before the change, first Hikari ERROR at 09:54:29Z, all 233 occurrences with total=5/active=5/idle=0/waiting 22-57
portfolio-service latency/error step to ~4.1-4.3s and 22% at 1-minute resolution: p99 flat ~172-178ms through 09:52, jumps at 09:53:00Z, error rate jumps at 09:54:00Z

api-gateway steps in the SAME 1-minute buckets (p99 200.33 -> 4418.76 at 09:53:00Z; error rate 0.30% -> 7.18% at 09:54:00Z) and never precedes portfolio-service, i.e. gateway latency is inherited from the upstream

The apparent 09:48 onset (F8) is a coarser-bucket edge artifact: re-bucketed at 120s the gateway error_rate at 09:48 is 0.28/0.31 = baseline, and the 60s series shows the collapse only at 09:53/09:54 — so the collapse does NOT precede the 09:52:00Z config stamp
api-gateway records upstream timeouts attributed to portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings and returns 504s, with flat gateway CPU (no gateway-side resource fault)

ledger-db metric side-effects are purely downstream: connections_active DROPS (61.8 -> 54.5) because portfolio-service holds fewer DB connections, while slow_queries, CPU, replication_lag and redis connected_clients are flat — no shared-dependency degradation

assumptions: Config apply latency is negligible: the pool rebuild takes effect within the same minute-to-few-minutes of cfg-2207. This is bracketed by telemetry (09:50Z partial bucket avg 9.17/max 12.22, pinned at 5.0 from the 09:55Z bucket) but the sub-minute rebuild instant is not directly observable — the config API exposes only changed_at and no apply/reload record (F38, F42, F43).
The ceiling value of 5 is inferred from cfg-2207 plus the observed pin at exactly 5.0, not read from a db_pool_max_size metric (which does not exist, F26).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Gateway HTTP/2 upstream upgrade (dep-5220) introduced a stream/connection handling regression
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-5220 (api-gateway v9.3.0, envoy 1.29->1.30, HTTP/2 to portfolio-service and order-service upstreams) shipped at 08:00Z changed upstream connection/stream handling and caused the portfolio-path p99 spikes and 504s. This is the reporter's stated suspicion. It remains rejected: there is a 1h52m quiet gap of flat ~200ms gateway p99 with no rollback before the single-minute onset (200.33 -> 4418.76 at 09:53), gateway CPU is flat across the whole window, the timeouts are attributed downstream to the portfolio-service upstream, and portfolio-service's failure signature is exactly JDBC pool exhaustion pinned at the new ceiling of 5 with Hikari 3000ms acquire timeouts — a mechanism a transport change cannot produce. The upgrade was never rolled back and nothing about it changed at 09:52-09:54Z.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5220 enables HTTP/2 to portfolio-service upstream at 08:00Z
HTTP/2 stream/connection handling to upstream is altered, degrading portfolio-path requests
Upstream requests to portfolio-service slow/fail, driving gateway p99 and error-rate steps at 09:52-09:54Z
Gateway logs 504 upstream timeouts for /v1/portfolio/*
Downstream, portfolio-service shows JDBC pool exhaustion at its new 5-connection ceiling while servicing these requests

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The upgrade's 08:00Z timestamp is 1h52m before onset and it was never rolled back, with a perfectly flat ~200ms gateway p99 (and flat ~172-178ms portfolio-service p99) across the whole intervening period (F33, F34, F35). Gateway CPU is flat across the entire 09:00-12:00Z window (F12). The original '09:48 onset' that could nominally align with the deploy is shown to be a coarser-bucket artifact; at 1-minute resolution the collapse begins at 09:53/09:54Z, hours after the deploy (F32, F35). The dominant failure signature is an upstream timeout attributed to portfolio-service (F9), and portfolio-service's own mechanism is JDBC pool exhaustion pinned at exactly the new ceiling of 5 with 3000ms Hikari acquire timeouts (F10, F11, F29, F30) — a transport-tier regression cannot produce DB-pool saturation. The one hop connecting the HTTP/2 change to portfolio-path degradation is unevidenced and no gateway envoy/stream/socket stat was ever retrieved.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared dependency (ledger-db and/or redis-cache) degraded independently at ~09:52Z
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared component on the portfolio path — ledger-db (shared by order/payment/settlement/auth) or redis-cache — began responding slowly at ~09:52Z, independently of the config change. Slow queries would hold portfolio-service JDBC connections, filling the pool and producing the 3000ms acquire timeouts and gateway 504s; the 5-connection ceiling would merely have removed headroom. Ruled out by dependency telemetry: ledger-db slow_queries_per_min (~1.0), cpu_pct (~30), replication_lag_ms (~40ms) are flat at 09:52Z and connections_active DECREASES (61.8 -> 54.5, wrong direction for DB-side overload); redis connected_clients is flat (~310, if anything lower at onset); ledger-db had zero config changes in the window. The pool never needed external pressure to saturate because baseline concurrency already exceeded 5.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db or redis-cache begins responding slowly at ~09:52Z
portfolio-service JDBC connections are held by slow queries, consuming pool slots
Pool (ceiling 5) reaches active=max, idle=0, with a waiter queue
Requests time out at Hikari's 3000ms threshold, raising portfolio-service latency to ~4s
Gateway reports upstream timeouts/504s on /v1/portfolio/*

assumptions: Residual: redis-cache hit_ratio_pct, evictions_per_min and cpu_pct were never retrieved (budget exhaustion), so a redis hit-ratio/eviction fault is not fully excluded — but a redis fault would not produce JDBC pool exhaustion on portfolio-service.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: F21/F22/F23 show ledger-db slow_queries_per_min, cpu_pct and replication_lag_ms flat at 09:52Z with no step; connections_active DECREASES (61.8->54.5) rather than rising, which is consistent with portfolio-service holding FEWER DB connections after the shrink, not with slow/long-held queries. F24 shows redis-cache connected_clients flat across 09:44-10:00Z with no step. F41 shows ledger-db had zero config changes in the window. F31 shows the pool saturation is explained by baseline concurrency (~11.4-12.4) already exceeding the new ceiling of 5, so no external connection-holder is required. The mechanism (slow query holds connections) is directly contradicted by the absence of any slow-query, latency or connection-rising signature on the shared components.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Gateway connection/socket or memory exhaustion as a co-factor (resource exhaustion at the gateway)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The gateway itself exhausted a finite resource (sockets/connections/memory) at ~09:52Z, stalling upstream request handling and timing out on portfolio requests, possibly enabled by the HTTP/2 transport change. Refuted by: gateway CPU flat across the window, 504s explicitly attributed in logs to the portfolio-service upstream (not a gateway-internal stall), and portfolio-service's own verified pool-exhaustion signature at its new 5-connection ceiling.

causal_chain.claim: Gateway exhausts connection/socket or memory resources around onset
Gateway stalls upstream request handling to portfolio-service
Gateway p99 and error rate step up
504 upstream timeouts logged for /v1/portfolio/*

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: F12 shows gateway cpu_pct flat (~41-43%) with no step at 09:48/09:52. F9 attributes the dominant failure signature (252 of 254 WARN) to 'upstream timeout portfolio-service' — the slow endpoint is the upstream, not the gateway itself. F34/F36 show portfolio-service steps in the same or the preceding 1-minute bucket, i.e. the gateway latency is inherited. F10/F11 show the actual failure locus is portfolio-service's saturated JDBC pool. If the gateway were the seat of exhaustion, its own resource metrics would move and the timeouts would not be uniformly attributed to one upstream.

facts.statement: cfg-2207 changed portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z (author infra-automation, description 'Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource'). It is the only portfolio-service config change in 06:00-11:59Z and the only config change on the portfolio path in the window other than a benign order-service log-sampling tweak at 07:00Z.

Only one deployment occurred across all services on 2026-03-10: dep-5220, api-gateway v9.3.0 at 08:00:00Z ('Upgrade envoy filter chain; enable HTTP/2 to upstreams', envoy 1.29->1.30, upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service). Status live, rolled_back_at null - never rolled back. There is no portfolio-service deployment at any time that day.

The gateway deploy is 1h52m before the 09:52Z onset, while cfg-2207 at 09:52:00Z lands in the same bucket as the latency step - the pool shrink is the last and only change to a portfolio-path service at onset.
Zoomed to 1-minute resolution, api-gateway latency_p99_ms is flat at ~200-210ms through 09:52:00Z (avg 200.33) and jumps to avg 4418.76 at 09:53:00Z, holding 4228-4624ms.

api-gateway error_rate at 1-minute resolution is flat at baseline (0.13-0.31%) through 09:53:00Z and steps in a single minute at 09:54:00Z (7.18%), holding ~6.8-7.4%; there is NO elevation at 09:48 (0.31%). The apparent 09:48 onset was a coarser 4-minute bucket-edge artifact.

portfolio-service shows the identical step: latency_p99_ms ~172-178ms through 09:52, jumping to 4250.91ms at 09:53:00Z; error_rate 0.17-0.28% through 09:53, jumping to 22.3% at 09:54:00Z. Both services degrade in the same 60s bucket and the gateway never precedes its upstream.

portfolio-service logs show JDBC connection-pool exhaustion: 270x 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' and 233x 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting 22-57)'. The 3000ms acquire timeout matches the ~4s p99 step.

portfolio-service db_pool_in_use is pinned at exactly 5.0 (max 5) from the 09:56Z bucket onward through 11:55Z, down from a stable ~11.4-12.4 average (max 13.3) before 09:48 - the pool is fully saturated at its new ceiling with zero idle for the entire incident.

Pre-change concurrency (~11.4-12.4 avg, max 13.3 in use) already exceeded the new ceiling of 5 by ~2.3x, and request_rate is flat across the window (08:00 bucket avg 543.14 vs 09:52 avg 560.3 vs 11:52 avg 573.87; mean 565.91) - saturation is driven by the reduced ceiling, not by a traffic increase.

There are ZERO ERROR-level log entries at portfolio-service in the pre-change window 08:00-09:52Z; the first 'Connection is not available' ERROR appears at 09:54:29Z and all 233 occurrences fall in 09:54:29Z-11:58:36Z, every one with total=5, active=5, idle=0.
Gateway 504s are logged as upstream timeouts attributed to portfolio-service, first at 09:53:53Z: 252 of 254 WARN entries match 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v<n>/portfolio/holdings'.
api-gateway cpu_pct is flat across the whole 09:00-12:00Z window (avg ~41-43%, max 46.78) with no step - no gateway-side resource saturation accompanies the latency step.

ledger-db health metrics are flat through 09:52Z: slow_queries_per_min ~1.0 (09:52 avg 1.01/max 1.31), cpu_pct ~29-30.7 (09:52 avg 30.5), replication_lag_ms ~39-41ms (09:52 avg 40.07/max 41.91); ledger-db had zero config changes in the window.

ledger-db connections_active does NOT increase at 09:52Z; it DECREASES from ~61-63 (09:44 avg 61.82, max 63.4) to avg 54.47 (max 58.04) and holds ~54-56 - the opposite direction to DB-side overload, consistent with portfolio-service clients holding fewer connections after the pool shrink.
redis-cache connected_clients is flat across 06:00-12:00Z (mean 310.28; 09:44 avg 314.6, 09:52 avg 304.29), if anything slightly lower at onset - no connection-count step.

The /v1/portfolio/* path is api-gateway -> portfolio-service (http) -> {ledger-db, market-data-service, redis-cache}; ledger-db and redis-cache are shared components with telemetry, but portfolio-service exposes no db_pool_waiting, db_pool_idle or db_pool_max_size metric (only cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts), so waiters/idle are readable only from Hikari log lines.

The config registry exposes only a changed_at field with no separate apply/reload/audit record, so the effective pool-rebuild time can only be bracketed by telemetry: the 09:50Z partial bucket reads avg 9.17/max 12.22, then the pool is pinned at exactly 5.0 from the 09:55Z bucket - a rebuild within ~09:50-09:55Z.

Precedent leads exist for both candidate changes (HIST-115 config-change pool exhaustion resolved by reverting config; HIST-116 gateway envoy HTTP/2 resets resolved by rollback), so precedent alone does not discriminate; neither history was treated as evidence here.

assumptions: Assumption: config apply latency for cfg-2207 is negligible, i.e. the pool rebuild took effect within the same minute-to-few-minutes of the 09:52:00Z stamp. This is bracketed by telemetry (09:50Z partial bucket avg 9.17, pinned at 5.0 from the 09:55Z bucket) but the sub-minute rebuild instant is not directly observable (F38, F42, F43).
Assumption: the effective ceiling value is 5, inferred from cfg-2207 plus the observed pin at exactly 5.0, since no db_pool_max_size metric exists (F26).

Assumption: no unqueried scale/HPA event between 08:00Z and 09:52Z affected the pool; this could not be verified because no HPA/scale query tool was available (config changes and deployments were confirmed absent for portfolio-service).

Assumption: redis-cache does not have a hidden fault that could produce portfolio-service JDBC pool exhaustion; redis is confirmed flat only on connected_clients (hit_ratio_pct, evictions_per_min and cpu_pct were never retrieved).

Assumption: the ~4s p99 step is fully explained by the 3000ms acquire timeout plus ordinary request handling overhead, not by an additional unobserved latency source; only pooled-connection acquisition timing is directly evidenced.

timeline.event: Only deployment in the window ships: dep-5220, api-gateway v9.3.0, envoy 1.29->1.30, HTTP/2 enabled to portfolio-service and order-service upstreams. Never rolled back.
1h52m quiet period: gateway p99 flat ~200ms, portfolio-service p99 flat ~172-178ms, gateway CPU flat, zero ERROR-level logs at portfolio-service, no config or deploy on the portfolio path.
Apparent coarser-bucket error_rate 'elevation' at the gateway (F8); at 1-minute resolution this bucket is still baseline (0.31%), so the reading is a bucket-edge artifact.
Partial db_pool_in_use bucket spanning the config change reads avg 9.17 / max 12.22 - pool concurrency falling toward the new ceiling.
cfg-2207 applied: portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5. Last and only change on the portfolio path at onset.

True onset: portfolio-service latency_p99_ms jumps to 4250.91ms (from 172.69) and api-gateway latency_p99_ms jumps to 4418.76ms (from 200.33) in the same 60s bucket; gateway does not precede its upstream.
First portfolio-service log signature of JDBC pool exhaustion ('could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms').
First api-gateway 504 logged as 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v<n>/portfolio/holdings'.
error_rate steps in a single minute: api-gateway 0.30% -> 7.18%, portfolio-service 0.26% -> 22.3%; holds thereafter.
First HikariPool 'Connection is not available, request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting 22-57)' ERROR at portfolio-service.
db_pool_in_use pinned at exactly 5.0 (max 5.0) in every 5-minute bucket for the rest of the window - sustained saturation at the new ceiling.
Incident INC-002 reported by on-call SRE (gateway p99 > 4s, 504s on /v1/portfolio/*); reporter suspects the earlier gateway HTTP/2 upgrade.
Latest data: gateway error_rate still ~7.1-7.4%, portfolio-service pool still saturated, no rollback of dep-5220 and no revert of cfg-2207 observed.

recommended_actions.action: Revert cfg-2207: set portfolio-service db.pool.max_size back from 5 to 50 (i.e. remove the 'cost-optimisation profile small' datasource override) and confirm the change is applied to the live pool.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2207 is the root cause: baseline concurrency ~11.4-12.4 (max 13.3) exceeds the new ceiling of 5 by ~2.3x, and the pool pins at exactly 5.0 with Hikari 3000ms acquire timeouts starting only after the change. Reverting restores the pre-incident ceiling with no code change.

recommended_actions.action: During the revert, monitor portfolio-service db_pool_in_use, latency_p99_ms and error_rate plus api-gateway latency_p99_ms/error_rate and the 504 rate; expect the pool to drop below 5 in use, waiters to clear, and p99 to return to ~200ms baseline within a few minutes (allow for the same minute-to-few-minute apply bracket seen on the way in).
recommended_actions.rationale: Verifies both the fix and the causal claim; the rebuild took effect within ~09:50-09:55Z on the way in, so a comparable recovery window is expected.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back dep-5220 (api-gateway v9.3.0 HTTP/2 envoy upgrade) as the mitigation; if the revert above does not restore p99, then revisit - but only with gateway envoy/stream/socket metrics in hand, which are currently unresolvable.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 is contradicted by the 1h52m quiet gap, flat gateway CPU, flat gateway p99 through 09:52, and downstream-attributed upstream timeouts; the HTTP/2->pool-exhaustion hop is unevidenced. An unnecessary rollback adds transport-churn risk during an active incident.

recommended_actions.action: If p99 does not recover after the revert, pull the still-missing discriminators in this order: (1) redis-cache hit_ratio_pct, evictions_per_min, cpu_pct for 09:00-12:00Z; (2) ledger-db WARN/ERROR logs for 09:40-10:20Z; (3) a sub-minute (finest available) zoom of db_pool_in_use across 09:50-09:56Z. Escalate to the shared-dependency hypothesis only if one of these shows a step at onset.
recommended_actions.rationale: H3's only surviving variant is a redis hit-ratio/eviction fault, which was never measured; ledger-db already moves the wrong way (connections down, slow queries/lag/CPU flat), so redis data is the remaining cheap discriminator. None of these can dethrone H1 unless they show a real step.

recommended_actions.action: Right-size the datasource profile for portfolio-service from measured concurrency rather than a generic 'small' profile: require peak baseline concurrency + headroom (observed ~12-13 in use) as the floor for db.pool.max_size, and document the sizing rule.
recommended_actions.rationale: The change was applied without reference to the service's actual ~11.4-12.4 (max 13.3) steady-state connection usage, guaranteeing saturation under unchanged demand.

recommended_actions.action: Add pre-apply guardrails to the config platform: reject or require explicit acknowledgement for datasource/pool-size changes that set pool max_size below the service's observed p95/p99 connection usage, and require a service owner (not only infra-automation) to approve.
recommended_actions.rationale: This was an automated 'cost-optimisation profile small' application that no human validated against live concurrency; a p95-based guard would have blocked it.

recommended_actions.action: Close the observability gaps that slowed this investigation: expose db_pool_max_size/db_pool_waiting/db_pool_idle as first-class time series, add a config apply/reload event (or a config-reload counter) so stamped-vs-effective time is observable, and add route-level metric dimensions so /v1/portfolio/* can be isolated.
recommended_actions.rationale: The conclusion rests on the pool pinning at exactly 5.0 and on Hikari log lines because pool ceiling/waiting/idle metrics do not exist and the config tool has no apply timestamp; endpoint-level breakdown is also absent.

recommended_actions.action: Replace or harden the change-ordering discipline in the incident runbook: on a same-minute latency step, diff config changes and deployments on the affected path at 1-minute resolution before chasing the loudest earlier deployment (the '09:48 onset' bucket-edge artifact sent the initial suspicion to the 08:00Z gateway upgrade).
recommended_actions.rationale: The apparent 09:48 onset was a coarser-bucket artifact; at 1-minute resolution the collapse begins at 09:53/09:54Z, strictly after cfg-2207, which correctly re-pointed causation away from dep-5220.

data_gaps: No ledger-db query-latency or error_rate metric exists (only connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min), so DB-side query latency/errors could not be measured directly; ledger-db health rests on slow_queries_per_min and replication_lag_ms proxies.

No db_pool_waiting, db_pool_idle or db_pool_max_size metric exists for portfolio-service; waiters (22-57), idle=0 and the ceiling of 5 were recovered only from Hikari log lines and the exact 5.0 saturation pin, not from a max_size time series.

redis-cache hit_ratio_pct, evictions_per_min and cpu_pct were never retrieved (tool budget exhausted), so the H3 rejection for redis-cache is partial - a hit-ratio collapse or eviction spike at 09:52Z cannot be excluded, though it would not by itself produce JDBC pool exhaustion on portfolio-service.

No HPA/scale/autoscale event query was available, so the absence of a scal-ing event affecting portfolio-service between 08:00Z and 09:52Z could not be verified by direct query (config and deployment absence were verified).

The config API exposes only a single changed_at field with no apply/reload/audit record, so the effective pool-rebuild timestamp for cfg-2207 cannot be separated from the 09:52:00Z stamp by tooling; only telemetry bracketing (09:50 partial bucket, 09:55 pin) is available.

No metric resolution finer than 60s exists, and the 09:52Z db_pool_in_use bucket is a 5-minute aggregate spanning the config change, so the exact within-minute collapse from ~12 to 5 and the sub-minute ordering of config apply vs first failing request cannot be resolved.

Gateway connection/socket/stream (envoy) metrics were never retrieved - only cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts are exposed - so the claim that dep-5220 produced no transport-tier signature at onset rests on the absence of gateway p99/error movement and downstream-attributed timeouts, not on connection metrics. Gateway memory_pct was also not retrieved.

Neither api-gateway nor portfolio-service exposes a per-endpoint/route metric dimension, so /v1/portfolio/* could not be isolated in metrics; the 09:53 onset is measured on service-level aggregates, with the endpoint-specific corroboration coming only from the /v1/portfolio/holdings log lines.

Telemetry for external nodes exchange-api, bank-partner-api and kyc-provider is unavailable (has_telemetry:false), and gateway ERROR-level log retrieval was truncated/level-filtered, so an unknown-signature contribution from those hops cannot be fully enumerated.
No restarts/reload counter was sampled finely enough to confirm by metric that no process restart accompanied the pool rebuild (no per-restart event log was retrievable).
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Reverting cfg-2207 (db.pool.max_size back to 50) fails to clear the saturation: if db_pool_in_use stays pinned at 5 with waiters persisting and p99 stays ~4s after the revert, H1 is false and attention must shift to H2/H3.

A redis-cache step at ~09:52Z in the unmeasured series (hit_ratio_pct collapse, evictions_per_min spike, or cpu_pct saturation) that could hold or starve portfolio-service requests would revive H3 as a co-cause.

A ledger-db signature at onset not visible in the retrieved metrics - e.g. a query-latency spike or error burst in ledger-db logs for 09:40-10:20Z, or a failover/blip matching the HIST-102 precedent - would revive the shared-dependency hypothesis.

Gateway-side envoy/stream/socket evidence showing connection or stream exhaustion (max concurrent streams, upstream connection resets) beginning at 09:53Z would restore H2 as a contributing cause; note a transport fault alone still cannot explain total=5/active=5 PoolExhaustion unless it induced connection-hold behavior.

Discovery of an earlier, unlogged pool-affecting event for portfolio-service (a scale/HPA event or a config apply not returned by the registry) between 08:00Z and 09:52Z that already lowered the effective pool size or raised concurrency would break the change-to-onset ordering.

Sub-minute telemetry showing the first Hikari acquire failure strictly BEFORE 09:52:00Z (i.e. before cfg-2207's stamp) would falsify the causal ordering, indicating the pool was already failing for another reason.

Evidence that baseline concurrency actually stayed below 5 (contradicting the ~11.4-12.4 avg / max 13.3 pre-change db_pool_in_use) would remove H1's core mechanism, since the 5-connection ceiling would then have headroom.

Proof that pre-change ERROR-level pool-exhaustion logs existed (contradicting zero ERRORs in 08:00-09:52Z) would show the pool was already stressed before the change and weaken attribution to cfg-2207.

findings.statement: Dependency graph: the /v1/portfolio/* path from api-gateway is api-gateway -> portfolio-service (http) -> {ledger-db (db), market-data-service (http), redis-cache (cache)}; market-data-service also calls redis-cache and exchange-gateway -> exchange-api (external, no telemetry). All services on the path have telemetry.

Shared components in the blast radius: ledger-db, redis-cache and kafka are flagged "shared":true. ledger-db is used by auth-service (user-db is separate), order-service and payment-service as well as portfolio-service; redis-cache is used by auth-service, market-data-service and pricing-engine. A neighbour can therefore hurt portfolio-service through these.

Exactly one deployment across ALL services in 06:00-11:59Z: dep-5220, api-gateway v9.3.0 at 2026-03-10T08:00:00Z, 'Upgrade envoy filter chain; enable HTTP/2 to upstreams' (envoy 1.29 -> 1.30; upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service). Status is 'live' with rolled_back_at null — it was NOT rolled back.

Mechanism match: cfg-2207 sets portfolio-service's pool max_size to 5, and T1 observed portfolio-service db_pool_in_use pinned at exactly 5.0 (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=25-57) from 09:56Z, down from a ~12.0 average before 09:48 — the post-change ceiling of 5 equals the observed saturation value, and the Hikari 3000ms acquire timeout matches the ~4s p99 step. The pool shrink is on the exact code path (/v1/portfolio/holdings -> ledger-db) that the 504s are attributed to.

The gateway deploy's HTTP/2 scope explicitly covers portfolio-service and order-service upstreams ('upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service'), so it does touch the portfolio path's upstream connection handling — but it is a transport/protocol change, not a connection-pool or DB-connection change, and it predates onset by ~1h52m with no intervening rollback.

The small 10:00-10:16 blip (1.17-1.22) is ~+20% and coincides with the incident, not a step change.

The DB never approached a connection ceiling — this is consistent with portfolio-service clients holding/serving fewer DB connections after the pool shrink, not with DB-side overload.

Interpretation: the dependency evidence REJECTS H3 (shared ledger-db and redis-cache degrading independently at ~09:52Z). Every available ledger-db metric (slow queries, connections, CPU, replication lag) and redis connected_clients is flat or moving the wrong way (DB connections DOWN) at the 09:48-09:52 onset buckets, with no error/step signature on either shared component. Because ledger-db/redis-cache show no degradation while portfolio-service p99 stepped (F10) simultaneously with the DB-connection-pool exhaustion signature, the flat dependency metrics demote H3 and are consistent with a portfolio-service-local cause (H1, cfg-2207 pool shrink at 09:52Z), with the 09:52 ledger-db connection drop being a downstream consequence of portfolio-service's pool being capped at 5 rather than a cause.

portfolio-service exposes no db_pool_waiting, db_pool_idle or db_pool_max_size metric: its full metric set is ['cpu_pct','db_pool_in_use','error_rate','latency_p99_ms','memory_pct','request_rate','restarts']. Only db_pool_in_use is available, so 'waiting' and 'idle' can only be read from Hikari log lines, not from metrics.

Pre-change (08:00-09:45Z) portfolio-service db_pool_in_use sat at a stable ~11.4-12.4 average (max 13.3) with zero missing points, i.e. well above 5 but nowhere near any visible ceiling, and with no trend. findings.statement: The 3000ms acquire timeout is a hard per-acquire ceiling, not a per-connection hold: waiting counts stay bounded (22-57) while acquisitions keep failing, and the post-change db_pool_in_use metric is exactly 5.0 with max 5.0 in every bucket — pool never holds more than the 5-permitted connections at once. Connections are not being held past the 3000ms bound; requests are simply queueing and timing out at 3s.

findings.statement: Answering H1's load-bearing assumption: pre-change concurrency (db_pool_in_use ~11.4-12.4 avg, max 13.3) already EXCEEDED 5 by ~2.3x, so the pool at max_size=5 would be saturated even at the old, unchanged request rate. The saturation is therefore driven by the reduced ceiling pulling below baseline concurrency, not by a rise in concurrency (request_rate flat) and not by connections held for the full 3000ms timeout (waiting bounded 22-57, in_use pinned at exactly 5). This supports H1 over H3's held/blocked-connection mechanism.

Both services step in the SAME minute and the gateway step FOLLOWS the portfolio-service step by zero-to-one minute but in no case precedes it: portfolio-service latency_p99_ms rises at 09:53 (4250.91) and api-gateway latency_p99_ms rises at 09:53 (4418.76), i.e. the downstream service degrades in the same 60s bucket as the gateway, consistent with the gateway latency being inherited from its upstream.

In the pre-09:52Z window 08:00-09:52:30Z, portfolio-service had ZERO config changes: the config query scoped to portfolio-service and bounded to 08:00:00Z-09:52:30Z returns count 1, and that one is cfg-2207 itself at changed_at 09:52:00Z — nothing earlier touches its datasource or pool.

No portfolio-service deployment exists at any time on 2026-03-10: the deployment query scoped to portfolio-service over 00:00-11:59Z returns count 0, and the all-services query over 08:00-09:52Z returns exactly one deployment, api-gateway dep-5220 at 08:00:00Z (status 'live', rolled_back_at null). So no restart or deploy touching portfolio-service's datasource preceded or accompanied cfg-2207.
ledger-db (the shared DB behind portfolio-service's failing path) had zero config changes in 06:00-11:59Z, so no pre-09:52Z config event on the shared dependency either.

The config API returns no apply/reload/audit event distinct from the config record: a broad 'config stamp vs actual apply delay / reload / restart / pool rebuild' precedent search returned only HIST-102 (portfolio timeouts during ledger-db failover, match_score 0.5), which is about a DB failover, not about config effective-time semantics. So there is no tooling evidence in this environment for an effective-vs-stamped time offset for cfg-2207.

Inference: because the config registry carries only the 09:52:00Z stamp and no reload event, the effective pool-rebuild time can only be bracketed from telemetry — consistent with F27 (09:50Z partial bucket avg 9.17/max 12.22, then pinned at exactly 5.0 from the 09:55Z bucket) the rebuild took effect within ~09:50-09:55Z, i.e. within a few minutes of the stamp, not hours later. This does not by itself prove the stamp equals the effective time.
